The central carbon atom of fenestranes has this molecular geometry, and reactions of substituents of complexes with this geometry are greatly accelerated when the trans ligand is a good pi acceptor. In crystal field theory, the d-orbitals of these complexes are split into four levels, giving it larger stabilization energy than the octahedral configuration. This geometry is occupied by low-spin d-8 complexes like Vaska's complex, the chemotherapy drug cisplatin, and a hydrogenation catalyst with a central rhodium atom and a series of triphenylphosphine ligands named for Wilkinson. According to VESPR, xenon tetraflouride occupies this configuration since it has 2 lone pairs and 4 ligands. Name this molecular geometry which is flat with four sides.

One method to detect these phenomena is a 68 centimeter sphere cooled to 20 millikelvin, while another one designed by Thorne, Drever, and Weiss consists of an L-shaped Michelson interferometer with Fabry-Perot cavities. Besides the miniGRAIL experiment, another apparatus used to detect them is a series of aluminum cylinders isolated from outside vibrations, named for Joseph Weber. The orbital decay of the Hulse-Taylor binary system is predicted to be due to these phenomena radiating energy away from the system, and they are radiated by accelerating, non-spherically or cylindrically symmetric system. The LIGO experiment attempts to detect, these phenomena predicted by general relativity.

Johnson and Pratt re-analyzed the original samples from this experiment and found hydroxylated products. This experiment immediately preceded Sydney Fox's experimental discovery of proteinoid microspheres, and Roscoe Stribling repeated this experiment with one of the original scientists. Originally designed to test a hypothesis of Oparin and Haldane, the apparatus contained a heated flask of water linked in series to a trap containing a sampling probe, a vacuum pump, and a chamber containing two electrodes. The chamber contained a mixture of water, methane, ammonia, and hydrogen cyanide, and this experiment was successful in creating sugars and amino acids. Name this experiment that was used to show that a pre-biotic Earth can create the precursors of life.

In cardiology, the value of this parameter increases with radius and decreases with wall thickness according to Laplace's Law. Knowing three vectors for this quantity in mutually perpendicular planes at a point allows for it to be calculated for any plane through that point according to Cauchy's theorem. Cauchy also lends his name to the second-order tensor used to represent this quantity, which has the normal ones on the diagonal and the shear ones off the diagonal. This value can be represented by Lame's ellipsoid but more commonly the normal and shear components are plotted against each other to find Mohr's circles. When this value passes the yield point, deformation occurs, and the ratio of it to strain is given by Young's modulus. Like pressure, it is represented as force per unit area. Name this measure of the intensity of forces acting on a deformable, solid body.

Both methyl orange and methyl red contain a diazo bridge para to one of these functional groups. Benzenesulfonyl chloride is used in a chemical test to detect this functional group named for Hinsburg, and a method of removing this functional group involves adding excess methyl iodide and heat. A popular method of synthesizing them involves the addition of an alkyl halide to potassium phthalamide. Adding one of them to formaldehyde is the first step of the Mannich reaction, and the previous reactions are the Hofmann elimination and Gabriel synthesis. Quaternary ones carry a positive charge, and aniline is a simple aromatic one. Primary, secondary, and tertiary ones have a lone pair. Name this functional group which contains a nitrogen atom single bonded to carbon chains.

The fact that the sea level had a highstand in the mid-Cretaceous can be explained by "pulse" in this process. This theory was first tested in measurements attempting to confirm the Vine-Matthews Hypothesis. Arthur Holmes presaged this model by postulating that convection cells could drive this process, which was confirmed by looking at the magnetic striping of rocks around ridges. Harry Hammond Hess helped confirmed this mechanism, which apparently functions more through slab pull than ridge push. This process occurs through upwelling of magma at mid-oceanic ridges, which are accommodated by subduction. Name this process that drives continental drift.

Georg Nagel isolated one of these proteins from Chlamydomonas which is linked to a nonspecific cation channel. Deisseroth's group switched out the intracellular domain of one of these proteins with an adrenergic receptor, creating OptoXR. Those proteins, known as the "channel-" type, are commonly used in optogenetics, while the "bacterio" type is used as a proton pump. This protein, when activated, decreases the concentration of cyclic GMP via the activation of transducin. Its cofactor changes into an all-trans state upon activation of this protein; that cofactor originally adopts an 11-cis confirmation and is known as retinal. Name this transmembrane protein found in photoreceptor cells, responsible for converting light energy to cellular signals.

One disease resulting from mutations in this protein causes destruction of small blood vessels in the kidneys and is called Alport Syndrome. It possesses repeating Glycine-X-Y motifs with the glycine facing the inside. Mutations in one type of this substance cause osteogenesis imperfecta, and its synthesis is inhibited by a low intake of Vitamin C, leading to scurvy. This fibrous glycoprotein forms a triple helix and is characterized by high tensile strength, and their mineralized form makes up bone matrix. Name this most abundant protein in mammals, which makes up connective tissue.

The radial part of the state vector for this system is given by a Laguerre polynomial while the angular portion is given by the spherical harmonics. Hyperfine splitting in it results in the 21-cm line, and solving this system requires separating the radial, angular, and azimuthal parts of the Schrodinger Equation. It produces series of lines such as the Paschen, Balmer, and Lyman series, whose energy is proportional to the difference of one over n-squared as given by the Rydberg formula. Name this quantum mechanical system which is accurately described by the Bohr Model and consists of one proton and one neutron.

The Tysganenko mode describes this phenomenon, and the strength of this phenomenon at a particular distance from its origin is described by the McIlwain L-parameter. Courtillot was the first to measure "jerks" in this phenomenon, while the K-index is used to measure other disturbances in this phenomenon. Anomalies in this phenomenon include the South Atlantic Anomaly and the Kursk Anomaly, and every few million years it undergoes reversals, which can be seen in the geological record. Its shape is dictated partially by its interaction with the solar wind. Name this phenomenon which arises due to currents in the outer core, whose strength is on the order of microteslas.

A group at Penn State recently created sheets of graphene from silicon carbide using this process. The primary drying phase of lyophilization occurs via this process since the pressure of the sample is lowered, and in most laboratory syntheses of ferrocene, the final product is purified using this process. Napthalene undergoes this process at room temperature, and in most laboratory apparatuses for performing this technique, it occurs on the surface of a cold finger. This process occurs at pressures and temperatures less than the triple point, and the enthalpy of this process is the sum of the enthalpies of fusion and vaporization. The opposite of deposition, name this process that occurs in solid iodine and dry ice, the direct transformation of a solid to a gas.

Sloane and Plouffe defined the "super" version of this function, while the number of un-rooted binary trees with a given number of leaves can be found using the "double" version of this function. Brute-force-searching the travelling salesman problem can be done in big O of this function. This function can be approximated as equal to the square root of two pi n times n to the n divided by e to the n, a method devised by Stirling. This function, which is applied to p minus 1 in Wilson's theorem, is most commonly used to find the number of permutations of n objects. Generalized by the gamma function, name this function symbolized by an exclamation point, equal to the product of all integers between 1 and the operand.
Facio-scapulo-humeral dystrophy is believed to be caused by these structures' namesake position effect,

Mutations in dardarin have been linked to some hereditary cases of this disease. One drug used to treat this disease is administered with a peripheral decarboxylase inhibitor in order to increase its half-life. One new treatment for this disease is deep brain stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus and globus pallidus interna. MPTP was linked to several instances of this disease in opiate addicts, and this disease is caused by a buildup of ubiquitin and alpha-synuclein-containing Lewy Bodies, which destroy the substantia nigra. Important symptoms of this disease include micrographia, cogwheel rigidity, and a mask-like facial expression. Commonly treated by L-Dopa, name this neurological disorder which causes impaired motor skills and eventually dementia, named for a British scientist.

A type of rock containing a high yttrium to strontium ratio known as adakite can form in the flat-slab type of these regions. A force affecting these regions contains a term equal to 4.2 times acceleration due to gravity and is known as slab pull. The emplacement of ophiolites is a result of the formation of back-arc basins in these regions. Seismic activity in these regions occurs in Wadati-Benioff zones, where megathrust earthquakes can occur due to significant accumulation of stress. A large example of these regions forms the boundary between the North American and Juan de Fuca plates and is the Cascadian one of these regions. Name these convergent plate boundaries where one plate sinks under another.

This property is the infinitesimal holonomy around a closed loop according to the Ambrose-Singer theorem. The asymptotic behavior of one quantity encoding this property is given by the big-O of the affine parameter to the negative fifth by the peeling theorem. One quantity encoding this property is decomposed into scalar, semi-traceless, and traceless components by the Kulkarni-Nomizu product. One half times the metric tensor times the scalar version of this quantity appears in one term of the Einstein field equation. One quantity used to define it can be expressed entirely in terms of the Christoffel symbols and their first derivatives. The Weyl tensor, the Ricci tensor, and the Riemann tensor all describe this property, which is zero for Euclidean geometry and negative for hyperbolic geometry. Name this quantity which produces gravity according to the theory of relativity, the deviation from flatness.

Mass spectrometry of these compounds can use the 2,5-DHB MALDI matrix, and these compounds are usually permethylated before MS. Alcian blue staining is used when conducting electrophoresis on these compounds. High-performance anion exchange coupled with pulsed amperometric detection is used to separate these compounds, which can be liberated using PNGase F. A mixture of carbonate, citrate, and copper (II) sulfate is used to detect these compounds with a free aldehyde on the end; that mixture is called Benedict's reagent and detects reducing types of these. Haworth and Fischer projections are commonly used to show their stereochemistry, and they commonly have carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen in approximately a 1 to 2 to 1 ratio. Name these macromolecules that include glucose.

Breakdown of this tissue is a feared side effect of the antibiotic daptomycin. It's not the skin, but a heliotrope rash, the shawl sign, and Gottron's papules are symptoms of a disease in which this tissue becomes inflamed. Satellite cells serve as quiescent stem cells in this tissue. Coenzyme Q10 supplements are used to prevent drugs like pravastatin from breaking down this tissue, a process called rhabdomyolysis. Myf5, MRF4, and MyoD are a series of basic helix-loop-helix transcription factors needed for differentiation of this tissue. The functional unit of this tissue is bounded by two Z lines, and contains thick filaments in the A band and thin filaments in the I band; that functional unit is the sarcomere, and contains actin and myosin. Name this tissue that comes in cardiac, smooth, and skeletal varieties.

One stochastic method for solving problems of this type adaptively estimates lower order moments, and is the Adam algorithm. One algorithm for solving these problems updates by setting the n plus first point equal to the nth point minus a constant times the gradient at the nth point. A naive algorithm for solving these problems involves repeatedly incrementing away from an arbitrary point, and seeing if the objective increases. Other algorithms for solving these problems include gradient descent and hill climb algorithms. Linear programming problems are a type of this problem which can be solved by the simplex method. Name these problems of finding the largest or smallest values obtained by functions.

Hinton and Zemel (zeh-mahl) used a function based on this quantity to compute recognition weights used to train an autoencoder. Two-sided estimation is used by the Bennett's acceptance ratio method to approximate this quantity. One relation states that this function for a liquid system is bounded above by a reference plus the difference between the Hamiltonians of the true and reference systems; that is the Bogoliubov (buh-GOAL-you-bahv) inequality. This quantity is minimized when a system is touching a thermal reservoir, and it is equal to negative Boltzmann's constant times temperature times the natural log of the partition function. This state function is the maximum amount of work obtainable from a reversible process and can be expressed as internal energy minus entropy times temperature. Name this non-Gibbs free energy.

This non-infectious disease is one of the few contraindications for the ParaGard IUD. A protein whose levels are used to diagnose this disease has the GAIT element in its 3' UTR (3 prime). T2 hyperintensities on brain MRI cause the "double panda sign" in sufferers of this disease. Trientine can be used to treat this disease in patients whose bone marrow is suppressed by the most common drug used to treat it. This disease, which can be diagnosed by low ceruloplasmin levels, is usually treated by D-Penicillamine. A classic sign of this disease is caused by deposits on Descemet's membrane that are visible under slit-lamp exam, called Kayser-Fleischer rings. It's my last Penn Bowl, so stop writing on this genetic disease caused by mutation of the ATP7B gene that causes buildup of copper.

A correction to this equation scales one variable as the normalized temperature to the 0.38 power; that correction relaxes the assumption that one quantity in this equation is temperature-independent and that correction is named for Watson. The August-Roche-Magnus formula is used to correct this formula when the saturation vapor pressure is temperature dependent. This equation is derived by noting that the chemical potential is equal across a phase boundary, then applying the Gibbs-Duhem relation. In one form, this equation is stated as the derivative of pressure with respect to temperature equals latent heat over temperature times change in specific volume. Name this doubly eponymous equation used to find the slope of coexistence curves.

They're not planets, but red-shifted absorption lines in the spectrum of beta pictoris were posited to be formed by these objects. JFCs and HTCs are subclasses of these objects, many of which are designated by a number, followed by a P, then a slash and a name. The Rosetta probe launched the Philae lander onto one of these objects. Remnants of these objects are responsible for the Orionids, Perseids, and Leonids, the last of which is caused by Tempel-Tuttle. Short period ones originate in the Kuiper Belt, and long period ones originate in the Oort cloud. Name these astronomical objects that contain an icy nucleus surrounded by a coma and tail, that include Hale-Bopp and one named for Edmund Halley.

This man names an effect in which shear stress on a granular material causes it to dilate. This man names a generalization of the Leibniz integral rule to three dimensions. An operator named for this scientist sets the velocity equal to a fluctuation term plus an average value. Relative roughness, the Darcy-Weisbach friction factor, and a quantity named for this scientist all appear on a Moody diagram. One quantity named for this scientist, whose namesake averaging is used to simplify the Navier-Stokes equation, is equal to velocity times linear dimension over kinematic viscosity and gives the ratio of inertial forces to viscous forces. Name this British scientist who names a quantity that's high for turbulent flow and low for laminar flow.

The absence of the HOX11 gene prevents this organ from developing. A disease whose two other main symptoms are rheumatoid arthritis and neutropenia has enlargement of this organ as a third symptom; that is Felty's triad. That enlargement of this organ can be found by percussing the lowest intercostal space and seeing if the note changes from resonant to dull. That is Castell's sign. Loss of this organ increases susceptibility to pneumococcus, meningococcus, and other encapsulated bacteria. The cords of Billroth are found in this organ and it is often enlarged and fragile in mononucleosis. Sickle cell anemia can cause sequestration of this organ, which is present on the left side of the abdomen. Name this organ whose white pulp synthesizes antibodies and whose red pulp filters red blood cells.

Jin-Quan Yu's group developed a series of MPAA derivatives used as these compounds in C-H activation reactions. Salicylaldehyde and an amine are condensed to form salen, which is often used as one of these compounds. The cube of the distance of closest approach of one of these compounds is found in the rate law for a reaction in which two of these things are exchanged, called the Eigen-Wilkins mechanism. These compounds decrease the B Racah parameter in the nephelauxetic effect. The number of contiguous atoms that one of these compounds uses to bond is designated eta and is called the hapticity. Those that bind to two centers are called bridging, and those that make more than one bond with one center are called polydendate. Name these compounds that bind to a central transition metal atom in a coordination complex.

Deletion of genes involved in this process was recently shown to inhibit white adipocyte differentiation and promote brown adipocyte transdifferentiation. MTOR (em-TOR) is thought to downregulate this process through phosphorylation of the ULK complex. Adaptor proteins for this process such as p62 and NBR1 commonly possess a LIR motif, which selectively binds to the Atg8 family of proteins. An assay for this process can be performed by immunoblotting for LC3-II turnover during the starvation-induced form of this process. The "macro" form of this process involves a formation of a double membrane around the cytoplasmic target, which can then fuse with the lysosome for degradation. Name this process in which a cell digests its own components for energy.

Mixing this compound with rhodium (III) chloride creates a complex used for cyclopropanation of alkenes, where this compound exists as a bridging ligand. One process for producing this compound occurs in an adiabatic flash tank and must stop precipitation of the tri-iodide intermediate. A vinyl derivative of this compound is polymerized into Elmer's glue. An anhydrous form of it forms crystals below 16.6 degrees Celsius and is commonly used for recrystallization. A square planar iridium catalyst is used in the main industrial process for manufacturing this compound. The Cativa and Monsanto processes produce this compound by carbonylation of methanol, and its pure form is called "glacial." name this acid found in vinegar.

A symmetrical lattice can be used to design a network of these objects with diagonally-crossed shunt elements; this expands on their ladder topology. Two opposing ones of these objects are added in the Linkwitz-Riley version of them. The Sallen-Key topology can be used to design these objects and calculate the poles and zeros of their transfer functions. These objects come in Chebyshev and Butterworth varieties. Their ringing and quality factor can be read from Bode plots of their magnitude and phase, which show minus 3 decibel gain at a cutoff value but can never be an ideal step function. The simplest types of these things are created out of a resistor and a capacitor, and can come in notch, band-pass, and high-pass varieties. Name these structures which remove unwanted frequencies from a signal.

One model for explaining the distribution of this quantity in the galactic disk assumes the instantaneous recycling approximation and ignores both infall and outflow. The non-existence of objects with low values of this quantity in the Closed-Box model is referred to as the G-Dwarf Problem. Objects with very low values of this quantity can hypothetically undergo runaway pair-production, resulting in core collapse. Hypothetical objects for which this value is zero are called "population III" and were created soon after the Big Bang. It is either symbolized Z or measured as the log base 10 of iron over hydrogen for the object in question minus said calculation for the sun. Name this property, the fraction of a star's mass that isn't hydrogen or helium.

If a class of objects named after this mathematician are simply connected, then they must be isomorphic to either another object named for this man, the complex plane, or the unit disk. Those objects are also the subject of a theorem he co-names with Roch. A problem named for this mathematician can be generalized to involve all Dirichlet L-functions. His namesake surfaces are connected complex manifolds of dimension one. A function named for this mathematician was expressed as an infinite product over the primes by Euler. That function evaluates to pi squared over 6 at two and to zero at all negative even integers. Name this German mathematician whose namesake hypothesis is a Millennium Prize problem.

Shifting the states of this system by x-sub-0 corresponds to the energy levels of cyclotron orbits in Landau quantization. A constant times the exponent of negative q squared over 2 gives the psi-sub-zero of this system, whose coherent states are named for Glauber. A pair of matrices whose superdiagonal and subdiagonal elements are the square roots of the natural numbers are used to move between energy levels of this system; those are symbolized a and a-dagger and are called the ladder operators. The energies of this system, whose wavefunctions contain the Hermite polynomials, are spaced h-bar times omega, and its potential is given by Hooke's law. Name this quantum system, a generalization of a mass on a spring.

One of these functional groups lies adjacent to a quaternary carbon in the antifungal terbinafine. As ligands, these compounds can act as either two- or four-electron donors. In the presence of nickel catalysts these compounds can trimerize into arenes. When they're hydroxylated they instantly transform into carbonyls by tautomerization. Two equivalents of hydrogen bromide can be used to transform them into geminal halides. Reacting these compounds with sodium metal dissolved in liquid ammonia gives the trans-alkene product, and they can be transformed into cis-alkenes via Lindlar's catalyst. These compounds contain two sp-hybridized carbons linked by one sigma and two pi bonds. Name this functional group that contains a carbon-carbon triple bond.

A model of this process was generalized by Gerola and Seiden and states that this process propagates through shockwaves generated by stellar winds; that model is SSPSF. An exponent of 1.4 is used to relate the rate of this process to the local gas surface density in the Kennicutt-Schmidt law. This process occurs in regions that have a high infrared excess in a color-color diagram. UV emission into H II regions can propagate this process. T tauri variables can result from this process, which commonly occurs in Bok globules. This process begins after the collapse of a giant molecular cloud, and the result of this process then moves along the H-R diagram. Name this process that mainly occurs in stellar nurseries.

The probability of a particle involved in this process existing before this process takes place is equal to the squared matrix element of the overlap of two wavefunctions and is known as the preformation factor. The kinetic energy of the product of this process is proportional to a quantity relating the masses of inputs to this process; that value is known as the Q-value. The probability of this process occurring can be calculated by applying the WKB approximation with a Coulomb potential; that model of this process is based on quantum tunneling and was developed by Gamow. The half-life is related to the energy released by this process according to the Geiger-Nuttall Law. This process decreases the mass number by four and the atomic number by two. Name this decay method in which an atom decays by emitting a helium nucleus.

One attempt to create a vaccine for this disease using a 42-amino acid-long peptide was halted in 2002 when it resulted in encephalitis in 6% of the trial patients. Later stages of this disease involve massive nitric oxide release from cells following activation of calcium-sensing receptor. NMDA receptor antagonists such as memantine are used to treat the late-stage symptoms of this disease. Down syndrome patients can exhibit early-onset of this disease due to the overexpression of APP. Arginine-112 and arginine-158 mutations in apolipoprotein E are closely linked to this disease. Tau tangles and beta-amyloid plaques are hallmarks of this disease. Name this most common neurodegenerative disease that results in dementia.

Systems without convection undergoing this process can show Liesegang rings. Ammonium sulfate is used to do this to proteins, and the Hofmeister series arranges salts by their ability to do this to proteins. Whether this process is reversed by the addition of KOH is useful for distinguishing primary or secondary amines in the Hinsberg test. Sodium acetate is used to coat DNA before subjecting it to this process using cold ethanol. The supernatant is what's left over after this process. This process can be triggered by adding an impurity to a supersaturated solution or adding a common ion, and occurs when the Ksp is really small. Name this process in which a solid falls out of solution.

With Sasaki and Ubeda, this scientist proposed the idea of "pacemaker islands" that restore genetic diversity in models of host-parasite evolution. This scientist used the life table of Taiwanese people to show how the forces of natural selection scale over age in one article. This scientist posited that secondary sexual ornamentation is a signal of disease and parasite resistance with Marlene Zuk. One result named for this scientist is usually formulated as "C is less than r times B", where r is the coefficient of relatedness. That result, first published in "The genetical evolution of social behavior", was summarized by J. B. S. Haldane as he'd die for two brothers or eight cousins. Name this evolutionary biologist whose namesake rule is used to quantify kin selection.

Note to players: the answer to this tossup is a function, like sine or the gamma function, but not those. One equation involving this function modifies another equation by including steric effects of substituents. This function of reaction rate plotted against this function of the equilibrium constant for a series of acids gives a line according to the Bronsted catalysis equation. Chemical potential is equal to k times T times this function of fugacity, and Gibbs free energy is equal to negative R times T times this function of the equilibrium constant. An expression involving this function is set equal to sigma times rho in the Hammett equation. This function is applied to a ratio of molarities in the Henderson-Hasselbach equation. Name this function that when applied to the concentration of hydrogen ions gives the negative pH.

Transport due to these entities is modelled by Peierls solution to the Boltzmann transport equation, which uses the relaxation time approximation. Klemens and Callaway name models for scattering due to these entities. Scattering of these entities in an inelastic manner increases thermal resistivity at high temperatures and is known as umklapp. For a basis of two atoms in the primitive cell, the type of these entities with a nonzero frequency at the center of the first Brillouin zone is known as their optical type. Multiplying the density of states of these entities by their energy, integrating up to their cutoff frequency, and differentiating gives a temperature-cubed dependence of heat capacity at low temperatures in the Debye model. Name these quasiparticles which correspond to the vibrational modes of a lattice.

In 2014, Srivastava et. Al introduced the idea of randomly removing components of these devices to improve their performance, a technique known as dropout. Some of these devices involve passing a filter over various parts of the input, and others have internal directed cycles which function as memory. Those are the convolutional and recurrent types of these devices, respectively. The McCulloch-Pitts model provided the inspiration for these devices, and they are the subject of an algorithm that iteratively uses the chain rule to compute a loss, the backpropagation algorithm. These devices consist of layers of hidden units stacked in between an input and output layer, with an activation function between each layer. For 10 points each, name these computational models often used in deep learning, named for their similarity to the structure of the human brain.

Richard Baraniuk developed the restricted amplification property in a "model-based sensing" algorithm named for this process, meant to optimize data collected for it. The Calgary and Silesia corpuses are used to test new algorithms of this type, one of which uses the move-to-front transform. One algorithm for this process constantly selects two characters of minimum frequency and merges them into one node. Another algorithm for this process finds the longest string in a table that is a prefix of the unscanned input; that is the Lempel-Ziv Welch algorithm. A binary trie is used to create an optimal prefix-free code in the Huffman form of this process, which can be lossless or lossy. After this process has been done to files, they may have the extension dot tar or dot zip. Name this process of decreasing the amount of data needed to store a file.

One experiment to measure a parameter involved in this process employs two gadolinium-doped scintillators at a nearly isoflux geometry which detect IBD events; that is the Double Chooz experiment. When two particles participate in this process, the probability of this process occurring is proportional to sine squared of 1.27 times the change in mass squared. This process was observed in an experiment which utilized a tank filled with 50,000 tons of water and 13,000 PMTs to detect Cherenkov radiation. That was Super-Kamiokande. The fact that this process occurs accounts for the discrepancy between the observed and predicted amounts of a certain type of particle emitted by the Sun. Name this process by which neutrinos change between electron, muon, and tau flavors.

Red pseudovesicular plaques and nodules in Sweet syndrome are caused by infiltration of these cells into skin. Mutations in the lamin B receptor causes the nuclei of these cells to take on a pince-nez appearance in the Pelger-Huet anomaly. C5a and LTB4 are chemoattractants of these cells, whose nuclei become hypersegmented in B12 or folate deficiency. Antibodies to HMG1, proteinase 3, and MPO are named for their staining pattern in the cytoplasm of these cells and are associated with small vessel vasculitis. These cells use NADPH oxidase and myeloperoxidase to produce hypochlorite in a respiratory burst, and these phagocytes are responsible for giving pus its green color. Name these most abundant white blood cells in the circulation, the first responders to infection.

BASF S6-10 catalysts are commonly used for this process. Alternatives to this process include the use of Molybdenum-HIPT catalysts in the Yandulov-Schrock cycle, and the catalyst most often used for it was developed by Alwin Mittasch. Gerhard Ertl won the 2007 Nobel for elucidating this process' mechanism, whose rate limiting step is adsorption to the iron catalyst. 3-5% of the world's natural gas is consumed in this highly exothermic process, which occurs at very high pressures in a classic application of Le Chatelier's principle. Name this industrial process which generates ammonia from nitrogen, developed by a German.

For a module M of a ring R, any alternating map out of R to the n can be written as the composition of a map corresponding to this quantity and a linear map. That map corresponding to this quantity is sometimes denoted with a wedge symbol. An alternating map applied to n vectors is equal to this quantity times that map evaluated at the basis vectors. This quantity is equal to the sum over all permutations sigma of the sign of sigma times the product of a sub i comma sigma i. This quantity is invariant under the transpose, and can be computed using expansion by minors. Name this quantity that for the two by two matrix with entries a, b, c, d is equal to a times d minus b times c.

One type of this technique requires a "purge gas" like nitrogen or helium to remove moisture and eliminate artifacts. The Joule effect is used to calibrate a device used for this process. Protonation effects must be considered in a form of this technique which measures ligand binding affinity by applying a feedback circuit to a system undergoing titration. Types of this device include the Tian-Calvet and the Sage form. Peaks signify the glass transition temperature by comparing reference and sample pans in the differential scanning form of this technique. The "bomb" form of this technique uses constant volume, while nested coffee cups can be used to conduct it at constant pressure. Name this instrument for measuring the heat produced in a reaction.

Mutations in FZD4, LRP5, or NDP can cause a genetic disease in which this structure shows exudates. Occlusion of its namesake vein creates a "blood and thunder" appearance. Atherosclerotic patients can have Hollenhorst plaques in the vessels found in this structure, which can cause amaurosis fugax. Ischemia (is-KEE-mi-a) in this structure shows up as cotton-wool spots. A lack of red reflex, or leukocoria, in children is indicative of a tumor of this structure, caused by mutations in RB. The choroid provides oxygen to the outer layers of this structure, which contains glia called Mueller cells. In this structure, bipolar cells communicate with ganglion cells. The fovea contains the densest concentration of cone cells in this structure. Name this thin layer of photoreceptors at the back of the eye.

This is the only dimension for which the smooth Poincare conjecture has not been resolved and the only dimension for which R to the n has an exotic smooth structure. In this many dimensions, isomorphisms of piecewise linear and smooth manifolds are the same, but different from isomorphisms of topological manifolds. The Hopf fibration is a map from a sphere in this many dimensions to a sphere in one fewer dimensions. This is the dimension of an algebra denoted H for its discoverer, Hamilton. The volume of a unit sphere in this many dimensions is pi squared over two. This is the minimum number of dimensions in which the Klein bottle can be embedded with no self-intersections. Minkowski space has this many dimensions since it models spacetime. Give the number of dimensions in a tesseract.

Severe necrotic lesions caused by this disease are called lues maligna. The Wasserman test for this disease has largely been replaced by the reactive-plasma reagin and VDRL tests. Clutton's joints and sabre shins are manifestations of one form of this disease, which can also manifest as interstitial keratitis, Hutchinson's teeth, and deafness in its congenital form. The causative agent of this disease shares a genus with the causative agents of bejel, pinta, and yaws. This disease is often diagnosed using dark-field microscopy or by detecting FTA antibodies. Its primary form is characterized by painful ulcerating lesions called chancres, and its tertiary form can cause insanity. Name this sexually transmitted disease caused by Treponema pallidum.

Adding terms governing this process due to the Bloch equation gives the Bloch-Torrey equation. An "apparent" coefficient governing this process is measured in a method in which each voxel is assigned a rate and direction; that method is used in tractography. In gases, this process's coefficient is equal to one-third times mean free path times mean thermal speed, and a law driven by this process sets a property's time derivative linearly proportional to its second spatial derivative. The Einstein-Smoluchowski relation finds this process's namesake constant proportional to mobility, Boltzmann's constant, and temperature. The flux due to this process is proportional to the concentration gradient, as stated in Fick's Laws. Name this process where particles move from areas of high to low concentration.

A spectral method for performing this process uses a set of equations written in terms of spherical harmonics that truncates at a wavenumber of 799. The results of multiple iterations of models used to perform this task can be visualized using a spaghetti plot. A dimensionless parameter called the Exner function can be used to simplify a set of equations governing this process. Numerical models used to perform this task may make use of a vertical coordinate system which is normalized by the surface pressure known as sigma coordinates. The results of this process are usually displayed on prognostic charts. Data is collected for use in this task by radiosondes which are carried by balloons. Modern methods of performing this task locate precipitation using the Doppler effect. Name this task performed by meteorologists.

The effect of these substances on elimination and substitution reactions is summarized in the Hughes-Ingold rules. When these substances are simply assumed to be a continuum, the change in free energy from adding one of them equals the sum of sigma times the accessible surface area. COSMO and Generalized Born are implicit models of these substances, whose strength is often given by their dielectric constant. The partition coefficient is used to determine when a compound will move from one of these substances to another. Rotary evaporation is used to remove these substances. Polar aprotic ones like THF are used for SN2 reactions, whose volume appears in the denominator of the equation for calculating molarity. Name these substances, of which water is considered the "universal" one, which dissolves solutes.

This technique is used to distinguish bridging and non-bridging ligands in metal carbonyl complexes and bent versus linear ligands in nitrosyl complexes. The DRIFTS version of this technique requires no sample preparation. Substitutions in a nickel carbonyl complex, in conjunction with this technique, are used to find a ligand's Tolman electronic parameter. A zinc selenide crystal is used in the total internal reflection variant of this technique; more commonly, samples are smeared on potassium bromide salt plates. The fingerprint region lies between 500 and 1500 wavenumbers in the output of this technique, which only detects vibrational modes that change the dipole moment. Carbonyls show up around 1700 wavenumbers in this technique. Name this form of spectroscopy that uses wavelengths longer than visible light.

Overdose of a drug that inhibits this protein is treated using fab fragments specific to it. A protein of the FXYD family associates with this protein to provide tissue-specific regulation. Ouabain and rubidium are often used to measure the activity of these proteins. Cardiac glycosides like digitalis inhibit this structure, which in turn inhibits NCX, creating increased calcium stores for more powerful heart contraction. This protein was discovered by Jens Christian Skou and has high affinity for certain ions before it is phosphorylated, but releases them afterwards. This transmembrane protein dephosphorylates an ATP to move three ions out of the cell and two ions in against their concentration gradients. Name this active transporter which maintains resting cell potential by moving Na+ and K+.

The trans form of one of these compounds binds more strongly to its receptor than the cis form, because it forms an additional hydrogen bond with the CHASE domain of that receptor. ABCG14 and AtPUP14 proteins are involved in the transport of these compounds. Prenylation of tRNAs is part of one pathway for producing these compounds. AHK2 and AHK4 bind strongly to the isopentenyladenine one of these compounds. These hormones are synthesized in the roots, and they promote root growth when there is a low ratio of these compounds to auxins. One of these compounds was discovered in coconut milk by van Overbeek; that is zeatin. Name this class of plant hormones which, as their name suggests, promote cell division.

Solutions to this equation have a corner if they meet the Weierstrass-Erdmann condition. For a disk sliding on a polymer brush, the coefficient of friction can be determined by solving the fractional form of this equation. For functionals that do not depend explicitly on the independent variable, this equation simplifies to the Beltrami identity. Solving this equation proves that the minimal surface for a soap film held at its ends by two wire rings is a catenoid. Finding a path for which the action is stationary is equivalent to solving this equation. The shape of the curve for which a bead accelerated from rest reaches the ground in the least time is determined by solving this equation for the brachistochrone problem. Identify this equation central to the calculus of variations, named for two mathematicians.

A list of maxims guiding the development of this language begins with "Beautiful is better than ugly" and "Explicit is better than implicit." That list can be accessed by running the code "import this" and is known as the Zen of this language. The seaborn library for this language can be used for data visualization, while the pandas library recreates much of the functionality of R in this language, which requires a reference to the instance variable "self" to be passed as the first argument to a method. The last version of this language to use print as a statement rather than a function was version 2.7. This interpreted language with "num" and "sci" libraries marks blocks of code with tabs or spaces, and does not end lines with semicolons. Name this language created by Guido von Rossum that takes its name from a John Cleese comedy show.

ARCH and GARCH conditions indicate that error terms for data points are correlated with other error terms that differ in this variable. In the weak efficient markets hypothesis, the rate of return of an asset is independent of this variable. A stationary process' statistical properties do not change with changes in this variable. The two components of an option's value are the intrinsic value and the [this] value. The auto-regressive integrated moving average, or ARIMA, is a common model applied to plots with this variable as the x-axis. Stock and flow variables measure quantities in relation to this variable. Effects in longitudinal studies and longitudinal data are observed over changes in this variable. Name this variable used in forecasting models in a namesake "series" from econometrics.

One theorem in this field states that under certain hypotheses, if a function g is strictly smaller than a function f on the boundary of a region, then f and f plus g have the same number of zeroes in that region. The fundamental theorem of algebra can be proven as a corollary of a theorem from this field by arguing that the reciprocal of a polynomial with no zeroes would have to be bounded, and thus constant. The main objects of study in this field satisfy the relations u sub x equals v sub y and u sub y equals negative v sub x. Those are the Cauchy-Riemann equations, which determine when a function is analytic, or equivalently holomorphic. Name this branch of mathematics that extends the results of real analysis to functions over C.

An integral-differential equation in the time domain can be used to analyze the behavior of a system undergoing the hysteretic type of this phenomenon. Another method for determining the extent of this phenomenon involves calculating the logarithmic decrement. For a series RLC circuit, the coefficient describing this process equals one over the resistance times the square root of the inductance over the capacitance. One quantity that describes the effect of this phenomenon equals two pi times the ratio of energy stored to energy dissipated per cycle and is known as the Q factor. When the coefficient describing this phenomenon is equal to the resonant frequency, it occurs in a critical fashion. Name this phenomenon which reduces the amplitude of a harmonic oscillator over time.

A family of receptors for this compound also contains members that bind to adiponectin and are called PAQRs. Ulipristal acetate is a selective inhibitor of this compound's receptors. This compound is converted to deoxycorticosterone by 21-alpha-hydroxylase and is synthesized by 3beta-HSD after side-chain cleavage of cholesterol. Devices called Skyla, Liletta, and Mirena elute an analog of this compound called levonorgestrel. A combination of a prostaglandin and an antagonist of this hormone's receptor, mifepristone, is used as emergency contraception. This hormone induces the formation of secretory endometrium after it is secreted by the corpus luteum post-ovulation. Name this hormone found in combined oral contraceptive pills along with estrogen.

During worship of Shiva, devotees often anoint themselves with this substance over parts of their body where the chakras are located; in that context, this substance is called vibhuti. Vaishnavites may use sandalwood paste in place of this substance to smear a "U" pattern. Kumkuma is a common red variety of this substance made from turmeric and slaked lime. Married women may adorn their hair partitions using a form of this substance called sindoor. Shaivites form three white horizontal lines with this substance, which is smeared onto a person's forehead to form a tilaka or tika (TEE-ka). In a legend that explains one use of this substance, Krishna used it to darken Radha's fair skin, which later evolved into gopis festively spraying water containing this on each other. For 10 point, name this substance people throw at each other during Holi.

Algorithms for finding these things are tested on OptBench, which includes the LJ38 and Heptamer Island test cases. The "climbing image" method is a modification of an algorithm used to find these things which adds spring forces along a pathway. Lorquet's nonadiabatic theory of these things allows for nonrelativistic coupling to cause mixed states. They are most commonly found using the synchronous transit or nudged elastic band methods, and they resemble the end state closest in free energy to them according to Hammond's postulate. They correspond to saddle points on a PES and are designated by a double dagger. The Arrhenius equation is used to find the energy of these things, which is called the activation energy. Name these locally-maximal energy intermediates in a chemical reaction.

The hyperpolarized isotope of this element is used as a contrast agent in magnetic resonance imaging to visualize gas flow through the lung. The trioxide of this element undergoes violent decomposition at only 77 degrees Fahrenheit, making it a highly explosive oxidizing agent in the +6 oxidation state of this element. In fast atom bombardment, atoms of this element are used to create ions in preparation for mass spectrometry. One structure involving this element has two axial unbound electron pairs when this element bonds to four fluorines to form a square planar compound. Discovered only weeks after krypton and neon, this element has an atomic mass of 131 and was named for being "strange". Name this noble gas below krypton on the periodic table, an element with symbol Xe.

The corkscrew model of these was described in a paper which aimed to discredit the histogen theory and was subtitled "lessons from the crypt". That population of these cells are surrounded by Paneth cells and intercalated columnar cells. Lineages of these cells can be traced by visualizing the polarity of the spectrosome or centrosome in Drosophila models. A theory of one type of these stem cells involves migration across an ovary while still retaining ring-canals between the lineage and is followed by a competitive selection mechanism. A series of high profile papers from the Spradling lab brought into question the definition of these cells, especially their supposedly dependent role on niche cells. Populations of these cells undergo asymmetric or symmetric divisions and can be replenished when transit amplifying cells dedifferentiate. For 10 points each, name these undifferentiated progenitor cells which include the embryonic and induced pluripotent types.

One method for modelling this technique shows that it's impossible at the plait point, and in that method an operating line is drawn on an equilateral triangle. Centrifugal contractors and mixer-settlers are used for this technique industrially, and it is modelled by the aforementioned Hunter-Nash method. One piece of laboratory equipment used to perform this technique should be vented by opening the stopper on top periodically during shaking, and like a buret has a stopcock on the bottom. This technique, which is commonly performed on DNA and protein using a mixture of isoamyl alcohol, phenol, and chloroform, is commonly used when the partition coefficient for a particular substance is much higher for an organic phase than an immiscible aqueous phase. Name this chemical technique in which a solute is transferred from one solvent to the other.

When deriving the Aharonov-Bohm effect, it is noted that the difference in phase between the two electron beams is invariant under this operation. This operation corresponds with rotating a vector for a given quark in color space in Yang-Mills theory. This operation, which corresponds to moving between two different sections of a principal bundle, leads to the conservation of charge according to Noether's theorem. These operations, which form a Lie group of their associated theory, leave the action invariant. This operation involves subtracting the time derivative of an arbitrary scalar function from the scalar potential and adding the gradient of that scalar function to the vector potential. Name this type of operation used in field theory which modifies the potentials without changing the fields.

One method of determining the distribution of this quantity quantum mechanically relies on partitioning it into spherical bains, a method named for Hirshfeld. This quantity is equal to Z minus GAP in a method that is prone to the appearance of excessively high off-diagonal terms in the P-matrix; that method is Mulliken population analysis. Redistribution of this quantity explains why trifluorocarboxylic acid is stronger than its unsubstituted version. This quantity, which is redistributed through bonds in the inductive effect, is often denoted by a lowercase delta with a plus or minus. This quantity is redistributed across a bond in which two substituents have differing electronegativities. Name this quantity whose total across an entire molecule is nonzero for ions.

These molecules accumulate in muscle and fibroblasts in people with Chanarin-Dorfman syndrome. A spike in both potassium and these molecules are characteristic of propofol infusion syndrome. Eruptive xanthomas are characteristic of a condition in which these compounds are elevated, called LPL deficiency. Fibrates are used to lower levels of these compounds, and an elevated level of them is one of the diagnostic components of metabolic syndrome. These compounds make up the majority of the lipids carried by a chylomicron, and high levels of them present an independent risk of coronary artery disease. Name these lipid molecules named for the fact that they contain three fatty acid chains linked to a single glycerol molecule.

Chevalley and Steinberg name extraordinary and twisted versions of these things, respectively. For the extension E/F, one example of these denoted Gal(E/F) can be given a Krull topology to be made into a profinite one of these. Another example of these is the collection of polygon symmetries, known as the dihedral ones of these structures. The geometry of four-dimensional conformal Minkowski space is defined by one of these according to the Erlangen program. The order of a substructure of one of these things divides the order of the parent structure according to Lagrange's theorem. The operation that defines this structure must satisfy the axioms of closure, associativity, identity, and invertibility. Name these algebraic structures where an operation combines two set elements into another element, one example of which is the set of integers under multiplication.

The HEALPIX algorithm was originally developed for studying this feature. Thomson scattering creates a linear polarization with vanishing divergence in this feature. The Eridanus supervoid may explain a "cold spot" in this feature. Primordial gravitational waves should imprint B-modes on the polarization of this feature. This feature, which was created from the surface of last scattering during the recombination era, was investigated by the COBE, WMAP, and Planck probes, which measured its anisotropy in order to test cosmic inflation. This feature was originally discovered by Penzias and Wilson in New Jersey. Name this radiation that permeates the universe, a relic of the big bang with frequency between radio and infrared.

Microscopic temperature gradients are introduced by these devices, which in turn induce changes in the hydration shell of macromolecules, in a method of measuring binding affinities called microscale thermophoresis. Small subpopulations of cells can be removed from a slide using a form of "capture microdissection" named for these devices. Continuous-wave types of these devices are used to induce changes in polarizability in Raman spectroscopy. These devices are often used to provide the "pump" in pump-probe spectroscopy; in those cases, these devices use chirped amplification to generate femtosecond pulses. Name these devices that generate coherent light through stimulated emission of radiation.

Expansions of the gut bacterium Prevotella copri are associated with the worsening of this disease. Disease activity in this condition is measured by the DAS28 score. Susceptibility to this disease is conferred by the HLA-DRB1 shared epitope motif. This disease, splenomegaly, and neutropenia make up Felty's triad. A combination of this disease and coal exposure can cause lung nodules, a condition called Caplan's syndrome. This disease is treated using DMARDs, some of which, like adalimumab and infliximab, inhibit TNF-alpha. This disease, whose symptoms include Z-deformities, swan-neck deformities and morning stiffness, has a namesake "factor", which is an IgM antibody that targets the IgG constant region. Name this autoimmune disease that causes pain and inflammation in small joints.

The vertical half-opening angle for collimated synchrotron radiation is inversely proportional to this quantity. In CGS units, this quantity appears raised to the sixth power in a generalization of the Larmor formula named for Lienard. This quantity is equal to the derivative of the coordinate time with respect to the proper time, and it is also equal to the hyperbolic cotangent of the rapidity. Multiplying this quantity times the time interval in the stationary frame gives the time interval in the moving frame. This quantity is equal to 1 at zero velocity. Name this "factor" equal to one over the square root of quantity 1 minus v squared over c squared, which is used as a relativistic correction for many quantities.

The nkd1 and nkd2 genes are named for the fact that mutations in them cause the outermost layer of this tissue to not develop. A sample of this tissue found in barley is used in an assay for gibberellins. Cotyledonous organisms do not retain this tissue beyond maturity of the organ in which it is stored. This tissue is generated when two polar nuclei fuse with one of the sperm nuclei from pollen, in a process of double fertilization. Amylase from the outer aleurone layer of this tissue digests the starchy portion of this tissue in cereal grains. Name this triploid tissue that nourishes the growing embryo inside a seed.

Gerald Sussman and Guy Steele coined the name for a technique used in this paradigm in which an extra argument is included to indicate what should be done after a routine has finished; that technique is continuation passing style. A technique called "currying," which is used to set the arity of certain constructs to "one," is used to implement first-class forms of the namesake things in this paradigm. Pattern matching is generally prevalent in this style, which often only evaluates a function argument if it is actually used due to "lazy evaluation." Technically, printing to a screen is not allowed in this style, since the "pure" form of this style avoids side effects. Languages which use this paradigm include ML, Scheme, and Haskell, and it is closely modeled on the lambda calculus. Name this programming paradigm, which views programs as the namesake mathematical constructs.

A multidimensional form of this technique is used in one stage of the MudPIT technique. An "Ultra" version of this technique was developed by the Waters corporation. Long-tailing of the peak of 2,2-bipy in this technique occurs when there is metal contamination. ESLD detectors can be used alongside this technique when the analyte isn't UV active. The composition of the mobile phase in this technique is continuously varied in its gradient elution mode, and is kept constant in isocratic flow. Originally invented by Csaba Horvath, this technique uses a packed bed with very small bead volume. Name this form of column chromatography in which the sample is forced through the substrate at high psi.

The anti-melanoma drug talimogene laherparepvec is an engineered form of this organism that secretes GM-CSF. This organism's UL30 polymerase associates with its UL42 processivity factor. This organism blocks the function of TAP using its protein ICP47. This virus is the most common viral cause of erythema multiforme. This virus can enter cells after binding to Nectin-1 of glycoprotein D, and its glycoprotein B and C bind to heparan sulfate. This virus can create whitlows on the fingers and hands. This virus encodes a thymidine kinase that is targeted by valacyclovir and acyclovir. This virus' latency associated transcript allows it to lay dormant in ganglia. Name this virus responsible for both genital lesions and cold sores.

The book Wonderful Life states that scientists will often describe Charles Doolittle as "that doofus who invented the non-existent Lipalian Interval to explain" this event. In a 1948 paper, Preston Cloud characterized a certain process as "eruptive" to explain this event. Many so-called "artifact" theories hold that this event only seemed to occur due to the prevalence of soft shells prior to it. This event may have been caused by a "methane burp" from the "clathrate gun" or by a combination of the rise of Hox genes and the reduction of aquatic bacteria, which led to higher oxygen levels in Earth's atmosphere. Name this event that took place roughly 540 million years ago, which was marked by the rapid diversification of lifeforms on Earth, named for the first period of the Paleozoic Era.

One method of calculating this quantity sets its log equal to f-oh plus f-1 times the acentric factor, where f-oh and f-1 are empirically-determined functions of the temperature with sixth power, log, and negative first power terms. The log of this quantity is equal to A minus quantity B over quantity C minus T according to the Antoine equation. The Goff-Gratch and Arden-Buck equations are empirical methods of calculating this quantity, which is also calculated by the Lee-Kesler method. Volatile substances have high values for this quantity at room temperature. This quantity is relevant when collecting a product "over water," and for each pure component of a solution it is equal to the total value for the solution times the mole fraction of the component, according to Raoult's law. Name this term for the pressure exerted by a gas in equilibrium with its liquid form.

One recent method for preparing this material involves using a simple sugar to synthesize it "bottom-up" with a controllable thickness; that is the Tang-Lau method, and it can be created from an intermediate called SLGO using hydrazine reflux. This material has a Berry phase consisting of massless Dirac fermions. This material has an anomalous half-integer quantum Hall effect. It is most often synthesized using chemical vapor deposition on metal surfaces, but it was originally created using scotch tape and is 100 times stronger than steel. Name this honeycomb-shaped structure, a single sheet of carbon atoms arranged hexagonally.

The 4F correlator is used in a field of optics that commonly employs this transformation, because the field radiated by a planar object is related by it to its point source. The power spectral density is related to the autocorrelation by this function according to the Wiener-Khinchin theorem. The Wigner-Seitz cell around the origin of a space defined as this function of the real space is known as the Brillouin zone; that space is known as reciprocal space. The basic form of Heisenberg's uncertainty principle can be derived by considering the change in the standard deviation of a Gaussian after being transformed by this function. A wavefunction can be transformed from position- to momentum-space by this function. Name this integral transform which takes functions from the time domain to the frequency domain.

A technique for performing this task uses correction passes based on the spectral response, and is named for Barnes. Shephard's method uses inverse distance weighting to perform this task. This task can be done by Gaussian modelling in a method called Kriging. Rarefaction is a form of this mathematical technique that uses subsampling, and oscillation at endpoints is a common artefact when using polynomials for this task, which can be avoided by using piecewise polynomial functions called splines. Name this method of constructing new data within the range of already existing data, often contrasted with extrapolation.

A type of these cells that localize to the subcapsular sinus express the antigen F4/80 in mice and express CD169 on their surface, and in germinal centers these cells can take on a "tingible body" appearance. Like helper T cells, these cells exhibit a form of polarization in which they can be either classically or alternatively activated. In Gaucher's disease, these cells take on a tissue-paper appearance, and using scavenger receptors they can take up oxidized LDL to become foam cells. These cells, like dendritic cells, differentiate from monocytes, and like dendritic cells and B cells they can use MHC II to present antigens on their surface. Name these leukocytes responsible for phagocytosis of debris and foreign antigens, with a name meaning "big eaters".

This species is transferred intramolecularly in ESIPT chromophores. 1,8 bis-dimethy-amino-napthalene serves as a "sponge" for this species. The transfer of this species is the fastest reaction in organic chemistry, which is why carbon nucleophiles are completely unusable in its presence. The transfer of this species to the ketone oxygen is one way of catalyzing keto-enol tautomerism. The "hopping" of this species generates the eigen and the zundel cations in the Grotthus mechanism. Solvents that are polar and lack this species are commonly used in SN2 reactions. The negative log of the concentration of this species gives the pH. Name this species, which Bronstead-Lowry acids donate.

The correlation between particle size and the activity of these substances was considered by van Hardeveld and Hartwig. The concentration of steps and kinks in these species are thought to influence their overall activity. Performing a material balance calculation at the pore of one of these substances gives a value that is the ratio of the rate over the diffusion constant. The productivity of these things is measured by their turnover number, and lead acetate is used to poison one of these named for Lindlar. They are classified as heterogeneous when they occupy a different phase than the species they act on. Name these chemical species that lower the activation energy of a reaction.

This man names an effect that arises in conductors whose bands are split by a magnetic field, resulting in a slight excess of spin in the lower band; that is his namesake paramagnetism. A set of mathematical constructs named for this man are multiplied by i to give infinitesimal generators of the group SU(2); those constructs are used to explain the interaction of spin with electromagnetic fields in three dimensions. One statement named for this physicist explains the electron degeneracy pressure found in white dwarves, and also explains why opposite spins pair in atomic orbitals. Name this physicist, the namesake of some spin matrices and a principle stating that no two fermions can share all of their quantum numbers.

Some oceanic structures, such as the Kerguelen Plateau and the Agulhas Plateau are mostly comprised of this rock. The accumulation of olivine and pyroxene in areas where this rock is formed can lead to the creation of Harzburgite. This rock has the same crystal structure, but is more mafic than diorite. Both the Emeishan Traps in Sichuan and the Deccan Traps in India are comprised of successive "floodings" of this rock. The "pillow" form of this rock, which is the extrusive equivalent of gabbro, comprises some of the ocean floor. Name this fine-grained igneous rock formed by the rapid cooling of lava.

Glycyrrhizic acid, which is found in licorice, increases the secretion of this ion. Low blood levels of this ion predisposes patients to digoxin toxicity and causes T wave flattening and U waves appearing on EKG. This ion is exchanged with hydrogen by ATP-driven antiporters in the wall of the stomach. In the islets of Langerhans, ATP-sensitive channels conducting this ion are closed in response to high glucose, triggering the release of insulin. Shaker channels in Drosophila conduct this ion. This ion exits the cell in the falling phase of an action potential. Name this cation that is exchanged with sodium by active transport in neurons in order to maintain resting membrane potential.

A pentadehydro modification of this reaction can be used to generate alpha-three-dehydrotoluenes. Derivatives of one reagent commonly used as a reactant in this reaction include ones named for Brassard and Rawal. Tetrahydropyridines are generated from imines in the aza form of this reaction. This reaction is particularly fast between cyclopentadiene and maleic anhydride, and this reaction preferentially generates the product generated when the electron-withdrawing groups on one reactant points inward, called the "endo" configuration. Name this [4+2] cycloaddition in which a six-membered ring is created from a diene and a dienophile.

The temperature equal to h-bar times gamma over 2 times Boltzmann's constant is the lower limit achievable using this effect. Saturated absorption spectroscopy is sometimes said to be "free" of this effect, which introduces a type of line broadening counteracted by the Dicke effect. An experiment in which canal rays were fired through perforated plates experimentally detected the transverse version of this effect; that experiment was conducted by Ives and Stilwell. This effect is used to measure the flow rate of blood through ultrasound, and in astronomy it is the basis for redshift. Name this effect in which the frequency of a wave decreases as the source moves away.

Donsker developed an extension of this theorem applying it to diffusely scaled random walks. In certain cases, the divergence of this theorem from its predicted result is given by the Berry-Esseen theorem. An extension of this theorem states that multiplying a large enough number of variables will result in a log-normal distribution leading to Benford's Law. This theorem is often used to justify the applicability of a sample size of greater than 30, and its proof is similar to the proof of the law of large numbers. Name this theorem which states that the sample mean of any independent random variable will be normal if the sample is large enough.

This reaction can be modelled by the GRI-mech program, and models of this process include Spalding's eddy break up model, which assumes fast reactions after the pre-heating phase. For most substrates, this reaction requires one reactant to undergo a forbidden transition from a triplet state to a singlet state. Smoldering is an example of its incomplete variety, and these reactions commonly occur at temperatures greater than the flash point. This reaction requires a fuel and an oxidant, and devices that use this reaction have exhaust products that are broken down by catalytic converters. Name this type of reaction in whose complete version a hydrocarbons is completely broken down into carbon dioxide and water.

Sleator et al performed an optical version of this experiment in which resonant and non-resonant helium atoms appeared to behave differently; that optical variant can be used to make non-demolition measurements. This experiment was assisted by the sulfurous output of a cheap cigar turning a photographic plate black. Although this experiment appeared to confirm the Bohr-Sommerfeld hypothesis over Larmor's theory, both were later shown to be incorrect. The experimenters never considered the atoms they used were in the L=0 versus the L=1 angular momentum states. In this experiment, silver atoms were accelerated through an inhomogeneous magnetic field, generating discrete spots on the detector. Name this experiment which showed that nuclei have quantized spin.

One of these devices contains about twelve thousand glass spheres resting on 600 glass strings at the bottom of the Mediterranean. One example of these devices contains a series of digital optical modules, and was used to find "double pulse", "sugar daddy" and "lollipop" signatures by the DONUT collaboration. A giant tank of perchloroethylene was used as one of these devices in the Homestake experiment, which detected approximately one-third of the expected number of particles being emitted by the sun. Name these devices that include IceCube and Super-Kamiokande, which detect a type of light uncharged particle that rarely interact with normal matter.

These organisms are infected by the tapeworm D. Robusta, and their milk contains the cathelicidin saha-CATH5, which kills MRSA. The strong jaws of this organism are similar to those of the hyena, an example of convergent evolution. These organisms are most closely related to quolls within the family Dasyuridae. Schwann cells from a single one of these organisms was found to be responsible for DFTD, a form of transmissible cancer affecting these animals that localized to the neck and face. These organisms preferentially eat carrion, and are about the size of a dog. Name these organisms, scientific name Sarcophilus harrisii, a carnivorous marsupial native to an island south of Australia.

One hypothesis for this body's low thermal flux proposes that a supermassive impactor made it lose most of its primordial heat. One layer of this body may be characterized by "diamond-bergs" floating on an ocean of liquid carbon. This planet's magnetopause is located at about 18 times its planetary radius and its magnetotail trails behind it in a unique corkscrew motion. The largest satellite of this planet is Titania, but its collective satellite system is the least massive of the group of planets it is a member of. This planet completes one revolution around the Sun about every 84 years and relative to the Sun's orbital plane, its axis is tilted at 98 degrees. Name this seventh planet from the Sun, a gas giant that appears to spin on its side as it orbits the Sun.

It's not an oxidation, but one type of this reaction has an intermediate in which a selenide is reacted with hydrogen peroxide to form a selenoxide. Tertiary amines are transformed into hydroxylamine in another reaction of this type. Those reactions are named for Greico and Cope. One mechanism for these reaction, which exhibits a very large deuterium isotope effect, is particularly fast when the substituents are in an anti-periplanar configuration. This kind of reaction preferentially generates the most substituted product according to Zaitsev's rule. Name these reactions that include E1 and E2, in which a functional group is "kicked out" of a molecule.
